question_text: If ax²+2hxy+by²+2gx+2fy+c=0 represents a pair of lines then prove that (a) Δ = abc+2fgh−af²−bg²−ch² = 0 (b) h²≥ab, f²≥bc, g²≥ac.

steps.why: This proof starts by SPLITTING the pair into its two separate lines with unknown coefficients, then matching coefficients against the given equation. Those matched coefficients, linking (a, h, b) to the two lines, are what every later step uses.
common_mistakes: Pairing the cross terms with the same subscript twice.
Forgetting that h, g and f are each HALF the matched quantity.

steps.margin_note: One mark. Each bracket becomes (sum)² − 2(product), and every one of those is already among the matched coefficients — so the expression can be written in a, b, c, f, g, h in one step.

steps.why: Δ = 0 is the first of the four conditions for a pair of lines, and this derivation shows it is not an arbitrary determinant but exactly what the splitting forces.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to divide the whole line by 4 at the end.
Sign slip when moving abc across.
steps.memory_tip: Each bracket becomes (sum)² − 2(product), and every one of those is already among the matched coefficients.

steps.label: Prove the inequalities
steps.margin_note: The last mark. h² − ab turns out to be a perfect square divided by 4 — and a square is never negative, which is the entire argument.

lines.text: (the same working with the pairs (g, a, c) and (f, b, c))
Similarly, g² ≥ ac and f² ≥ bc

recall.must_convey: That h² − ab equals (l₁m₂ − l₂m₁)²/4, which is a square and therefore non-negative.
accept: h squared minus a b is a perfect square over four so it cannot be negative
sum squared minus four times the product is the difference squared
a square is never negative so h squared is at least a b
square kabatti negative kaadhu
similarly for the other two
heard_as: h squared is at least a b

steps.why: The same argument runs unchanged for g² − ac and f² − bc, with the letters permuted, so writing 'similarly' is enough rather than setting it out twice more.
common_mistakes: Claiming strict inequality h² > ab, which fails when the lines are parallel.
Forgetting the division by 4 when writing h from 2h.
steps.memory_tip: h² − ab is a perfect square over 4 — and a square is never negative. That IS the argument.

lines_compact.text: Similarly, g² ≥ ac and f² ≥ bc

insider_note: Multiply 2h, 2g and 2f together, not h, g and f — that gives 8fgh, and dividing both sides by 4 at the end leaves 2fgh. Part (b) is short: h² − ab becomes (l₁m₂ − l₂m₁)²/4, so h² ≥ ab, with equality when the lines are parallel or coincident.
